title: Python SDK: event-driven streaming handoff API and ergonomic consumer patterns
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: Teams building streaming chat features report friction when integrating incremental events into application-level consumers. Current patterns in the Python SDK mix raw event iteration with ad-hoc checkpoints, making it hard to compose middlewares (retries, de-duplication, telemetry) and to implement clean handoffs between streaming and non-streaming code paths.

This ticket proposes a small, focused ergonomics surface for the Python SDK: an event-driven handoff/Router API plus a set of canonical consumer factories and examples. Goals: reduce boilerplate, make backpressure and soft-retry semantics explicit, enable idempotent handoff of partial responses, and provide clear examples that map to real app architectures (websocket relay, background writer, aggregator).
acceptance_criteria:
- New public API: StreamHandoffRouter (or similarly named) implemented in python SDK (stable preview).
- API supports: registration of named consumer handlers, explicit start/stop/handoff semantics, checkpoint tokens for resume, and a simple backpressure signal.
- SDK includes at least three example integrations: websocket proxy, append-only conversation writer with idempotency markers, and consumer that aggregates for downstream embedding.
- Unit tests covering emitter->router->consumer happy path, resume after disconnect, and single-retry soft-failure semantics.
- Documentation page + cookbook with minimal code examples and migration notes.
- Performance: added latency of router plumbing should be <200us median in microbenchmarks.
- Telemetry: tracing spans for handoff events and counters for retries/drains.
design_decisions:
- API shape: prefer small class with well-documented async iterator compatibility rather than monkey-patching existing stream interfaces. This keeps integration straightforward for both sync-adapters and async consumers.
- Use explicit checkpoint tokens (opaque strings) that the API returns; the SDK will not attempt to interpret them to keep forward compatibility.
- Backpressure: router exposes a simple `pause()` / `resume()` signal and a high-water mark that consumers can query; we avoid complex flow-control protocols in v1.
- Retry semantics: implement soft-retry built into consumer factories (idempotent retries with exponential backoff, capped attempts). Hard retries (server side replay) delegated to higher-level orchestration.
- Opt-in telemetry: default metrics emitted to Redwood SDK metrics surface; tracing hooks available for customers to map handoffs to request traces.
implementation_notes:
- Add new module `redwood.streaming.handoff` with router and consumer factory classes.
- Provide convenience adapter `from_event_iter()` that wraps existing generator-based streaming responses.
- Implement lightweight in-memory checkpoint store for examples; production users should plug their K/V store.
- Add typed stubs and docstrings for IDE discoverability.
- Keep public surface minimal for v1. Avoid adding complex state machines until we gather usage telemetry.
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2147 (WIP)
- Draft design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/py-sdk+streaming+handoff+patterns
test_plan:
- Unit tests for router lifecycle: register, emit, handoff, pause/resume, checkpoint/resume.
- Integration test using a fake streaming backend that yields interleaved content and sideband events; validate consumer receives correct sequence and resume token after disconnect.
- Load microbenchmarks to measure median added latency (<200us) using pytest-benchmark.
- Fuzz test for corrupted checkpoint tokens to ensure graceful failure.
rollout_notes:
- Feature gated under `stream_handoff_preview` flag for first release.
- Publish docs and a short migration cookbook.
- Early access to 3 internal SDK consumers and a small set of customers; collect feedback and telemetry for 2 sprints before GA.
- Plan for deprecation if we introduce a replacement API after experiment period.
